subject.title: 飞书话题群(Topic Group)被识别为p2p导致消息路由错误

question: Which Feishu/Lark signal should OpenClaw trust to classify `chat_type: "p2p"` events from `oc_...` conversations as group/topic messages, and should maintainers adopt, narrow, or replace the open fork PR?
rationale: Current source proves the bug, but current tests also prove that some p2p events with root/thread metadata must remain direct; choosing the permanent discriminator needs maintainer product/API judgment and likely Feishu contract or live proof.

options.title: Use a verified shared discriminator
options.body: Create or adopt a Feishu-local classifier that only promotes p2p events to group/topic when verified OpenChat/topic metadata is present, and reuse it in dispatch and mention-forward logic.

options.title: Accept the broad oc_ prefix rule
options.body: Adopt the open fork PR shape that treats p2p `oc_...` events as group, accepting the risk that ambiguous p2p/direct cases may move to group routing.

options.title: Wait for Feishu contract proof
options.body: Keep the issue open until a live Feishu/Lark replay or official API documentation confirms the exact topic-group event shape.

recommendation.title: Use a verified shared discriminator
recommendation.body: Create or adopt a Feishu-local classifier that only promotes p2p events to group/topic when verified OpenChat/topic metadata is present, and reuse it in dispatch and mention-forward logic.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent topic-session stabilization commit touched the same central Feishu dispatch, type, mention, and test surfaces.
